accepted_scope_caveats.label: All exact-class identification, computation, and coverage targets
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Finite rational grids, endpoint-anchored rational piecewise-affine quantiles, and rational piecewise-polynomial payoffs are assumed as an adopted or externally validated surrogate class, not inferred from finite calibration.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Every sharpness, compiler, and DKW claim is conditional on membership in the declared exact rational surrogate class; no physical-law misspecification claim is made.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 equates context-independent inverse transport with exogenous isomorphism under local invertibility; Theorem 2 gives arbitrary conditional counterfactual-query agreement; Proposition 1 gives failure under context-dependent transport.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Official proceedings abstract and bibliographic record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The ICML paper exists and studies exogenous-isomorphism sufficient conditions in bijective and triangular monotonic SCM classes.
The paper proves counterfactual identifiability for Markovian, IV, and backdoor bijective-generation settings under its listed assumptions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Official proceedings abstract and bibliographic record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper by Sourabh Balgi, Jose M. Peña, and Adel Daoud establishes c-GNF counterfactual equivalence under a monotonicity assumption.
The paper proves noninformative continuous-counterfactual bounds under broad smoothness and informative bounds under a curvature sensitivity model.
The paper canonicalizes discrete SCM inputs, produces an equivalent polynomial program, and supplies epsilon-sharp branch-and-bound ranges.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Official repository abstract and publication record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper bounds counterfactuals over nonparametric neighborhoods of latent distributions while holding structural features fixed, using finite-dimensional convex programs.
For iid observations, Massart establishes the sharp two-sided DKW bound 2 exp(-2 lambda squared).
The paper gives calibrated projection confidence intervals for smooth functions of finite-dimensional partially identified parameters with uniform asymptotic coverage.
Theorem 4 places almost-sure liminf and limsup of the neural partial-identification optimizer inside a Lipschitz-model interval, and explicitly does not generally guarantee point convergence.
The paper gives a general marginal-MAP dual representation and documents the noncommutativity of summation and maximization.
The paper studies tractability and intractability boundaries for pseudo-Boolean optimization on signed hypergraphs, including treewidth and nest-set-gap results.
The paper defines breakdown frontiers for nested relaxations and develops estimation and inference for them.
